Restating a blueprint lemma while a seat is working on the old version: the seat's file passes `check` against its creation-time template, but the splice breaks Blueprint.lean (t96A08 transfer, 10-13). land.sh now compiles the blueprint after each splice and reverts if it fails (exit 2). Requeue such lemmas with the old proof under partials/ as a starting point.

Compile-gate pitfall (10-14): `lean ... | grep -A6 error | head && git commit` commits even on error (head exits 0). Write output to a file and test `grep -c ": error"` = 0 before committing; and gate `lemmatool make` on the bank commit succeeding (a failed bank + make overwrote a seat's partial work).

Design trap (10-14, t02A01): a blueprint `def` whose body uses a sorry'd lemma (e.g. a subtype membership proof) makes every leaf about that def carry sorryAx, so the checker rejects proved leaves. Prove such membership facts inline in the def, or land that lemma first and reland the rest.

Seat compile claims are unreliable (10-14, Fmoves zipCone_continuous, zip_halfDisk_cone): a "PROVED, compiles" or "sorryAx remains" report can hide plain compile errors. Lean marks a declaration that fails to elaborate as sorryAx. The usual causes are swapped argument order in add_le_add_left/right, nonexistent names (Filter.nhds, ContinuousAt.subtype_mk), and positivity failing on a bound it cannot see is nonnegative. land.sh catches it. When the argument is sound, fix the names myself (minutes) rather than redispatching.

Own slip 10-14 (Fmoves 94c052f64): I banked a seat's "proved" helper and committed without checking the error count. The helper did not compile in the blueprint. Always gate blueprint commits: `[ "$(grep -c ': error' out)" = 0 ] && git commit`. When reverting, use the explicit pre-commit hash, never HEAD~1: next.sh commits seat files to the same branch in between, so HEAD~1 was my own bad commit.

Disk load (Joe, 2026-10-15): run few seats. `~/notes/packets/lemmas/SEATS` lists the seats next.sh may feed (3 to start); `PAUSE` stops all dispatch. Every Lean compile, in seats and in land.sh, goes through `flock /tmp/apm-lean-compile.lock`, so only one runs at a time.

Coordinate trap (t99A01, 10-15, three times in one problem): when leaves state equations "in coordinates", the coordinate isos must be canonical defs, built from the witnesses passed in as parameters. Never `∃ e, …` in one leaf and `(e : …)` arbitrary in another. Seats catch the resulting false or vacuous leaves; sign flips of an arbitrary H₀ ≅ ℤ are the typical counterexample.

Registry trap (10-15): `statement-registry.py admit` fingerprints the COMMITTED file (HEAD), not the working tree. Commit the statement change first, then admit, then commit STATEMENTS.json; an admit before the commit silently registers the old statement (m01J04).
futon3c test JVMs default to /tmp/futon3c-invoke-jobs.edn, the live Agency ledger path; run tests with FUTON3C_INVOKE_JOBS_FILE set to a temp path.
**Why:** with whole-file rewrites the clobber healed itself in 1.5 s; with append-only journals it doesn't, so a stray writer now matters.

The live Agency's invoke ledger uses the default path `/tmp/futon3c-invoke-jobs.edn` (FUTON3C_INVOKE_JOBS_FILE unset), and so do test JVMs. On 2026-10-12 05:02 one of my suite runs left a 102-byte empty ledger in place of the live 99 MB snapshot. Under the journal writer that persisted: a restart would have loaded an empty ledger and refused it. I repaired it from the live JVM (forced snapshot), and futon3c f7f8dff6 makes both journal writers re-snapshot when the snapshot's [file-key size mtime] changes underneath them.

**How to apply:** since futon3c cd33eebd the :test aliases redirect these defaults themselves (-Dfuton3c.test-run=true); for other runners, still run tests with `FUTON3C_INVOKE_JOBS_FILE=$(mktemp -d)/i.edn FUTON3C_DURABLE_QUEUE_PATH=$(mktemp -d)/q.edn` (pass them with `systemd-run -E`). The lasting fix, moving the live ledger out of /tmp via the unit's environment, is Joe's call at a restart. Related: [[proc-io-includes-reaped-children]], [[slow-tagged-tests-hide]].

The 09-27 statement-fidelity hold was answered by the 09-28 statement-registry gate (`scripts/statement-registry.py check`). Joe restarted the loops after that. Related: [[codex-default-model-astra]], [[zone-1-1-rebuild]].

**Before launching, register topo-1..8 yourself** (`POST /api/alpha/agents/restore`, with `"model":"gpt-5.6-sol"`). If they are missing, both loops auto-register at the same moment and collapse onto topo-1/topo-2: one seat ends up as owner, author and probe for both loops. Agency forgets seats when it restarts.

The loops are `apm-lean/holes/labs/topology-contract/topology-supervisor.sh`, run as transient user units `topo1` (worklist.edn, runs/) and `topo2` (worklist2.edn, runs2/) in `futon-agents.slice`. topo1 seats: owner topo-1, author topo-2, review topo-3, probe/strategy topo-4, repair topo-2. topo2 seats: topo-5/6/7/8, repair topo-6. Escalations go to claude-18, and `TOPOLOGY_SEAT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol`. The full `systemd-run` line is in this session's transcript (2026-10-10, claude-14). Stop with `systemctl --user stop topo1 topo2`; TERM keeps the in-flight job for reclaim.

legend.retrieved-only: named by m40_find in this turn; the statements were not read
legend.reached: its statements were returned by a recorded call in this turn
legend.echoed: the reply shares a run of five words, or the memory's name, with it
legend.in-force: the memory was said before the turn and not withdrawn by then
legend.retracted-since: the memory was in force at the turn but has since stopped being said
legend.not-yet-said: the memory was first said after the turn
